title: Orchestrated Right-to-Be-Forgotten: Automated Purge + Verification Workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver an end-to-end orchestrated Right‑To‑Be‑Forgotten (RTBF) workflow that: 1) accepts deletion requests via API/Console, 2) runs automated purge jobs across all retention surfaces (primary DBs, caches, KV cache, object storage, analytics derivatives, backups where feasible), 3) produces machine-readable and human-readable evidence packages that prove deletion, and 4) verifies purge completeness with periodic re-checks and an audit trail suitable for compliance reporting.

Scope: Customer-facing RTBF orchestration for Hosted and Dedicated customers. Private (on-prem/VPC) customers will receive the orchestration spec and control plane hooks; implementation in customer-owned infra is out of scope for this ticket. The initial rollout covers text generation request data, embeddings, and associated metadata (request timestamps, routing keys). Excluded for phase 1: aggregated usage metrics needed for billing (billing data handled via separate retention exception process) and immutable legal archives required by lawful retention holds (we will surface a manual review path).

Non-goals: Do not change default retention policies in this ticket; this work implements enforcement and verification of configured policies. Do not attempt to delete model artifacts or shared public content that are not derived from a customer identity.

Stakeholders: Legal (privacy@redwood.com), Security (sec-ops), Compliance PM, Infra/Runtime, Storage Engineering, Console UX, Customer Support, Solutions Engineering.

Success metrics: average end-to-complete purge time for small datasets (<10K tokens) < 1 hour for hosted customers; evidence package generation available immediately after purge completes; verification check passes within 24 hours and is rechecked 7 days later; audit report exportable (PDF + JSON) for a given request ID.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint /v1/privacy/delete accepts deletion requests with tenant_id, scope, and optional retention override flag
Orchestration runs purge subtasks across DB, object store, runtime KV caches, and analytics derivatives and returns a status object per surface
Evidence package contains: list of purged object keys/IDs, purge timestamps, purge job IDs, checksum/hashes where applicable, and signed audit entry
Verification job re-checks surfaces and fails the request if remnants are found; failures create SRE ticket and notify customer
Console shows per-request timeline (requested -> in_progress -> purged -> verified) and link to evidence package
Automated integration tests simulate a deletion request and assert no retrievable payloads via API/SDK within configured retention boundaries
All actions are logged to the immutable audit log stream with correlation_id for export
Legal sign-off on evidence package format and retention of audit metadata
implementation_notes:
Architecture sketch: a coordinator service (privacy-orchestrator) receives RTBF requests and creates a correlated purge run ID. The coordinator enqueues per-surface purge tasks to task-queue (Kafka/work-queue) and tracks heartbeats. Surfaces implement a purge adapter interface: purge(ids) -> taskStatus and generate evidence artifacts stored in secure S3 bucket with ACLs and KMS encryption. The verification worker kicks off after all surfaces report success and performs randomized tombstone scans and deterministic key checks. Evidence packages are signed with a service signing key and stored for export.

Key technical considerations: handling KV cache TTLs and in-flight KV cache entries (we must invalidate prefixes and drop prefix-index entries), expunging streaming/transient logs by redacting pointers, and ensuring eventual deletion from S3 lifecycle/Glacier where immediate purge is impossible — such cases must be surfaced in evidence with expected timeline. Backups: where immediate deletion from immutable backups is impossible, we must mark the request with a retention-hold-exception and include the expected restore-window and mitigation plan.

Telemetry: create metrics: purge_requests_total, purge_duration_seconds (histogram), purge_surface_failures_total{surface}, evidence_generation_duration_seconds, verification_pass_rate, verification_false_positive_rate. Dashboards and SLA alerts to be added to Console and PagerDuty playbooks.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (internal): implement orchestrator + DB + runtime KV + object-store adapters in staging; run synthetic RTBF runs against test tenants and validate evidence packages (2 weeks). Phase B (beta): expose API to 10 pilot customers, enable console UI with readonly evidence preview; collect feedback and run audits with Legal (3 weeks). Phase C (GA): enable self-serve RTBF via Console + API for hosted customers; provide implementation guide and automation hooks for Dedicated customers (2 weeks). Feature gating: defaults off; enable per-org via feature flag and require a signed legal attestation before enabling for production tenants.

Canary & testing: staged rollout by tenant region; monitor verification_pass_rate and purge_surface_failures_total during rollout. If verification_pass_rate < 98% for 24h, rollback to feature-off for newly received requests and open incident review.

Docs & training: publish PRD, runbook for support, and a short training session for CSMs/Support on how to interpret evidence packages and escalate to Security/Legal.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental data loss for data that should be retained for legal/billing reasons; Mitigation: require retention-exception flow with legal sign-off and clear confirmation UI before executing purge

Risk: incomplete deletion because of secondary derived datasets or exported analytics; Mitigation: include derived-data adapters and flag datasets as derived so they are included; where impossible, surface in evidence package

Risk: high-latency purges on very large customers causing missed SLAs; Mitigation: asynchronous response model + progress timeline + SLOs by size bucket; for very large jobs, offer Dedicated contract SLA
Risk: cryptographic verification tampering; Mitigation: sign evidence packages and store signatures in an immutable audit log (WORM) with KMS-protected keys and rotation policies
dependencies: DES-412 (console UI: deletion request flow & evidence viewer)
